title: Naming and Naming Conventions for Javascript Variables
summary: Rules and conventions for naming variables: which names JavaScript rejects, what characters are allowed, why meaningful names matter, and camelCase. Also shows how to clear the DevTools console versus truly resetting memory.

concepts.heading: Clearing the console versus clearing state
points: Cmd+K (Mac) or Ctrl+K (Windows) clears the console output only. Variables created earlier still exist, so typing myName still returns its value.

To wipe stored state, do a hard reload: hold the reload button (Mac) or right-click it (Windows) and choose Empty Cache and Hard Reload. Afterwards the old variable is gone (typing it gives a not-defined error).
(Extra) A plain page refresh in DevTools usually also discards variables from the page's memory, since a fresh page context is created.

concepts.heading: Hard rules (JavaScript enforces these)
points: Cannot be a reserved word: var var = ... is an error. A name may contain a keyword (myvar is fine).
Cannot start with a digit: 123 is invalid, but my123 is valid.
No spaces: my name would be read as variable my followed by a stray token.
Only letters, digits, $ and _ are allowed. my-name is invalid because the hyphen is read as subtraction, but my_name is valid.
(Extra) Names are case-sensitive: myname, myName and MyName are three different variables.

concepts.heading: Conventions (humans enforce these)
points: Choose meaningful names that make the contents obvious; strings of random characters work but make shared code unreadable. Compare folders labelled Pictures or Documents with folders called untitled folder 1 to 6.
Use camelCase: first word lowercase, each following word capitalised (userScoreFinal). Capital letters mark word boundaries so names stay readable.
A website domain example (a therapist-finder site) shows how running words together without case can be misread.

pitfalls: Using hyphens in names (kebab-case works in CSS, not JavaScript).
Starting a name with a number.
Thinking the console clear command also clears variables.
Assuming any name that runs is a good name.

playground.coverage: Good: camelCase, PascalCase, SCREAMING_SNAKE, cannot start with a number, reserved words, case-sensitivity, boolean/function naming tips, and a rename-the-bad-names task.
gaps_and_ideas: Add the specific rules about spaces and hyphens (my name, my-name) with a quick-fire 'valid or invalid?' task.
